cases.sentence: ___ был высокий и жирный человек, с одутловатым и бесцветно-бледным, гладковыбритым лицом.
cases.translation: Zosimov was a tall, fat man with a puffy, colorlessly pale, clean-shaven face.
cases.explain: «Зосимов» is the subject of «был», so it stands in the nominative case.

cases.sentence: Некто крестьянин Душкин, содержатель распивочной, напротив того самого ___, является в контору.
cases.translation: A certain peasant, Dushkin, keeper of a tavern across from that very house, comes to the office.
cases.explain: The preposition «напротив» (opposite) governs the genitive case, giving «дома».
The preposition «на» here governs the accusative case (direction of a gesture), giving «Раскольникова».

cases.translation: Razumikhin, banging his fist on the table, exclaimed.
cases.explain: The instrumental case here expresses the instrument used in «стукнув» (banging with), giving «кулаком».

cases.sentence: Это точь-в-точь как сначала они забрали и заподозрили этих… Коха да ___.
cases.translation: This is exactly like how, at first, they seized and suspected Koch and Pestryakov.
cases.explain: «Заподозрили» (suspected) is a transitive verb whose direct object takes the accusative case, giving «Пестрякова».

cases.sentence: А в комоде, в верхнем ___, в шкатулке, одних чистых денег на полторы тысячи нашли.
cases.translation: And in the chest of drawers, in the top drawer, in a box, they found clean cash alone worth fifteen hundred.
cases.explain: The preposition «в» marking location governs the prepositional case, giving «ящике».

reading.ru: Зосимов был высокий и жирный человек, с одутловатым и бесцветно-бледным, гладковыбритым лицом, с белобрысыми прямыми волосами, в очках и с большим золотым перстнем на припухшем от жиру пальце.
reading.question: How is Zosimov physically described?
options: Tall and fat, with a puffy pale face, wearing glasses and a gold ring
Short and thin, with a beard
reading.correct: Tall and fat, with a puffy pale face, wearing glasses and a gold ring
reading.explain: He is described as tall and fat, puffy-faced, pale, clean-shaven, wearing glasses and a large gold ring.

reading.ru: Все, его знавшие, находили его человеком тяжелым, но говорили, что свое дело знает.
reading.question: What did people who knew Zosimov generally think of him?
options: That he was a difficult person but knew his profession well
reading.correct: That he was a difficult person but knew his profession well
reading.explain: Those who knew him considered him a difficult man, but acknowledged he knew his own business (medicine) well.

reading.ru: Я здоров, я совершенно здоров! — настойчиво и раздражительно проговорил Раскольников, приподнявшись вдруг на диване и сверкнув глазами, но тотчас же повалился опять на подушку и оборотился к стене.
reading.question: How does Raskolnikov react when Zosimov asks about his health?
options: He insists irritably that he is completely healthy
He calmly admits he feels unwell
He falls silent and refuses to answer
He asks Zosimov to leave immediately
reading.correct: He insists irritably that he is completely healthy
reading.explain: He insists, irritably and with flashing eyes, that he is completely healthy.

reading.ru: Завтра вечером я его гулять веду! — решил Разумихин, — в Юсупов сад, а потом в «Пале де Кристаль» зайдем.
reading.question: What plan does Razumikhin announce for Raskolnikov's recovery?
options: To take him for a walk to the Yusupov Garden and then to the "Palais de Cristal"
To send him to a hospital
To take him to visit his mother
reading.correct: To take him for a walk to the Yusupov Garden and then to the "Palais de Cristal"
reading.explain: Razumikhin declares he will take Raskolnikov walking in the Yusupov Garden and then to the "Palais de Cristal" the next evening.

reading.ru: Эх досада, сегодня я как раз новоселье справляю, два шага; вот бы и он.
reading.question: What is Razumikhin celebrating that very evening?
reading.correct: A housewarming (novosele)
reading.explain: Razumikhin mentions he is having a housewarming party that very evening, just a couple steps away.

reading.ru: Порфирий Петрович придет: здешний пристав следственных дел… правовед.
reading.question: Who is mentioned as a guest coming to Razumikhin's party, who is also a local investigating official?
reading.correct: Porfiry Petrovich
reading.explain: Razumikhin says Porfiry Petrovich, the local police investigator and a lawyer, will be coming.

reading.ru: Скажи мне, пожалуйста, что может быть общего у тебя или вот у него, — Зосимов кивнул на Раскольникова, — с каким-нибудь там Заметовым?
reading.question: What does Zosimov question about Razumikhin's friendship with Zamyotov?
options: What Razumikhin or Raskolnikov could possibly have in common with someone like Zamyotov
Why Zamyotov is not invited to the party
Whether Zamyotov is trustworthy with money
Whether Zamyotov is a good doctor
reading.correct: What Razumikhin or Raskolnikov could possibly have in common with someone like Zamyotov
reading.explain: Zosimov asks what common ground Razumikhin (or Raskolnikov) could have with someone like Zamyotov.

reading.ru: Заметов человек чудеснейший.
reading.question: How does Razumikhin describe Zamyotov?
reading.correct: As a wonderful/splendid person
reading.explain: Razumikhin insists that Zamyotov is a "most splendid" person.

reading.ru: Да всё по делу о маляре, то есть о красильщике… Уж мы его вытащим!
reading.question: What case is Razumikhin excitedly discussing with Zosimov?
options: The case of the house painter accused in the murders
reading.correct: The case of the house painter accused in the murders
reading.explain: Razumikhin is talking about the case of the housepainter (implicated in the murders), whom he insists they will "pull out" (clear).

reading.ru: Лизавету-то тоже убили! — брякнула вдруг Настасья, обращаясь к Раскольникову.
reading.question: What shocking remark does Nastasya suddenly blurt out?
reading.correct: That Lizaveta was killed too
reading.explain: Nastasya suddenly blurts out that Lizaveta was also killed.

reading.ru: Раскольников оборотился к стене, где на грязных желтых обоях с белыми цветочками выбрал один неуклюжий белый цветок, с какими-то коричневыми черточками, и стал рассматривать: сколько в нем листиков, какие на листиках зазубринки и сколько черточек?
reading.question: What does Raskolnikov do to avoid reacting to the mention of Lizaveta's murder?
options: He turns to the wall and fixates on studying a flower pattern in the wallpaper
He gets up and leaves the room
reading.correct: He turns to the wall and fixates on studying a flower pattern in the wallpaper
reading.explain: He turns away to the wall and stares intently at a flower in the wallpaper pattern, trying to hide his reaction.

reading.ru: Это точь-в-точь как сначала они забрали и заподозрили этих, как бишь их… Коха да Пестрякова.
reading.question: Who were initially suspected of the murders, according to Razumikhin?
reading.correct: Koch and Pestryakov
reading.explain: Razumikhin recalls that Koch and Pestryakov were initially seized and suspected.

reading.ru: Некто крестьянин Душкин, содержатель распивочной, напротив того самого дома, является в контору и приносит ювелирский футляр с золотыми серьгами и рассказывает целую повесть:
reading.question: Who comes to the police office with a jewelry case containing gold earrings?
options: Dushkin, the tavern keeper across from the house
reading.correct: Dushkin, the tavern keeper across from the house
reading.explain: Dushkin, a peasant who runs a tavern opposite the house, brings in a jeweler's case with gold earrings.

reading.ru: Прибежал-де ко мне повечеру, третьего дня, примерно в начале девятого, — день и час! вникаешь? — работник красильщик, который и до этого ко мне на дню забегал, Миколай, и принес мне ефту коробку с золотыми сережками и с камушками
reading.question: Who brought the box with gold earrings to Dushkin, according to his account?
reading.correct: Nikolai, the housepainter
reading.explain: Dushkin reports that Nikolai, the housepainter, ran to him in the evening with the box of gold earrings.

reading.ru: За дверьми? За дверями лежала? За дверями? — вскричал вдруг Раскольников, мутным, испуганным взглядом смотря на Разумихина, и медленно приподнялся, опираясь рукой, на диване.
reading.question: What detail about the earrings' location visibly startles Raskolnikov?
options: That they were found lying behind the door
That they were found in the trunk
That they were found on the street
That they were found in Nikolai's pocket
reading.correct: That they were found lying behind the door
reading.explain: Raskolnikov cries out, startled, asking repeatedly whether the earrings were found lying behind the door.

reading.ru: Задремал, должно быть, спросонья, — проговорил наконец Разумихин, вопросительно смотря на Зосимова; тот сделал легкий отрицательный знак головой.
reading.question: How does Razumikhin explain away Raskolnikov's strange outburst?
options: He guesses Raskolnikov must have dozed off and reacted from half-sleep
He thinks Raskolnikov is angry at him
He assumes Raskolnikov wants more soup
reading.correct: He guesses Raskolnikov must have dozed off and reacted from half-sleep
reading.explain: Razumikhin explains it away, suggesting Raskolnikov must have dozed and reacted out of half-sleep.

reading.ru: Наступил на коробку и поднял!
reading.question: According to Nikolai's account (as retold by Razumikhin), how did he actually find the earrings?
options: He stepped on the box in the empty apartment and picked it up
He stole them from the old woman's trunk directly
He found them on the street, as he first claimed
reading.correct: He stepped on the box in the empty apartment and picked it up
reading.explain: Razumikhin recounts that Nikolai stepped on the box and picked it up in the apartment where he had been working.

reading.ru: Теперь строго заметь себе: тела наверху еще теплые, слышишь, теплые, так нашли их!
reading.question: What key detail does Razumikhin emphasize to argue Nikolai and Dmitri are innocent?
options: That the bodies were still warm when found, inconsistent with the two men's carefree behavior afterward
That the door was locked from outside
That no blood was found on their clothes
That witnesses saw the real killer leave
reading.correct: That the bodies were still warm when found, inconsistent with the two men's carefree behavior afterward
reading.explain: Razumikhin stresses that the bodies were found still warm, which contradicts the men's carefree, laughing behavior right afterward.

reading.ru: Это доказано, — отвечал Разумихин, нахмурясь и как бы нехотя, — Кох узнал вещь и закладчика указал, а тот положительно доказал, что вещь точно его.
reading.question: How was it proven that the box of earrings came from the old woman's trunk?
options: Koch recognized the item and identified the pawnbroker who confirmed it was hers
The police found her handwriting on it
Lizaveta identified it before she died
reading.correct: Koch recognized the item and identified the pawnbroker who confirmed it was hers
reading.explain: Razumikhin explains that Koch recognized the item and pointed to the pawnbroker, who confirmed it belonged to the old woman.

reading.ru: А коробку он выронил из кармана, когда за дверью стоял, и не заметил, что выронил, потому не до того ему было.
reading.question: According to Razumikhin's theory, how did the earrings end up in the empty apartment?
options: The real murderer dropped them there while hiding behind the door
Nikolai stole them from the murderer
The old woman had given them to the painters
Dmitri planted them to frame Nikolai
reading.correct: The real murderer dropped them there while hiding behind the door
reading.explain: Razumikhin theorizes that the actual murderer dropped the earrings from his pocket while hiding behind the door, not noticing it in the moment.

reading.ru: Хитро! Нет, брат, это хитро. Это хитрее всего!
reading.question: How does Zosimov react to Razumikhin's elaborate theory about the real killer's escape?
options: He calls it too clever/contrived, suspicious in how neatly it all fits together
He dismisses it as completely impossible
reading.correct: He calls it too clever/contrived, suspicious in how neatly it all fits together
reading.explain: Zosimov remarks that the theory is "too clever," suspicious because everything fits together so neatly, "like in a play."

reading.ru: Да потому что слишком уж всё удачно сошлось… и сплелось… точно как на театре.
reading.question: Why does Zosimov find Razumikhin's theory suspicious?
options: Because everything fits together too perfectly, like in a stage play
Because Razumikhin has no medical training
Because it relies entirely on hearsay
reading.correct: Because everything fits together too perfectly, like in a stage play
reading.explain: He explains that it's suspicious precisely because everything comes together too neatly, as if staged like theater.

reading.ru: Я Порфирия уважаю, но… Ведь что их, например, перво-наперво с толку сбило?
reading.question: What does Razumikhin say about his feelings toward Porfiry despite disagreeing with the investigation?
options: That he has never met Porfiry
reading.correct: That he respects Porfiry
reading.explain: Razumikhin states that he respects Porfiry, even while criticizing how the investigation was initially misled.

reading.ru: На рутину их дряхлую, пошлейшую, закорузлую злюсь… А тут, в одном этом деле, целый новый путь открыть можно.
reading.question: What does Razumikhin say he is truly angry about regarding the investigators?
options: Their decrepit, hackneyed, entrenched routine methods of investigation
reading.correct: Their decrepit, hackneyed, entrenched routine methods of investigation
reading.explain: He says he is angry at their decrepit, stale, entrenched routine, believing a whole new investigative approach could be found in this case.

reading.ru: Э-эх! — вскричал было Разумихин, но в эту минуту отворилась дверь, и вошло одно новое, не знакомое ни одному из присутствующих, лицо.
reading.question: What interrupts Razumikhin at the very end of the chapter?
options: The door opens and an unfamiliar new person enters
reading.correct: The door opens and an unfamiliar new person enters
reading.explain: Just as Razumikhin exclaims, the door opens and someone unknown to everyone present walks in.
